texts.facts: 3. The genesis of the complaint is that on 13.09.2015 at about 8.00 a.m. when the complainant was in police station, he received a telephone call stating that accused No.2 and other accused are involved in manufacturing and adulteration of milk by mixing chemical powder and trying to sell the same to the public. Immediately, the complainant along with his staff and pancha witnesses went to the said place and conducted a raid in the house of accused No.2. At that time, accused No.1 was also present there. There, they found one plastic bag, other materials and vehicles loaded with milk powders. On verification, they found that the accused No.1 was using mixer and mixing the powder with oil and mixing the said mixture into milk to increase the quantity. There were six empty cans which were kept for the purpose of filling the same. On enquiry, they came to know that the accused persons were mixing the powder with oil and thereafter increasing the quantity of milk by mixing the water. The said milk powder was intended to be supplied to Anganwadi schools in Karnataka. On the basis of the complaint, cases have been registered against the petitioners-accused persons. 4. It is the submission of the learned counsel for petitioners-accused persons that the other accused have already been released on bail during the crime stage itself, and the charge-sheet has already been filed in both the cases. On the ground of parity, these petitioners-accused persons are also entitled to bail. It is submitted that the alleged offences are not punishable with death or imprisonment for life and the petitioners-accused persons are ready to abide by all the conditions imposed by this Court and also ready to furnish the surety to the satisfaction of the Court. On these grounds, prayed to allow the petitions.
texts.arguments: 5. Per contra, the learned HCGP for respondent-state has vehemently argued and contended that the petitioners-accused persons along with accused Nos.1 and 2 have sold the milk which was intended to be supplied to Anganwadi schools by increasing the quantity by mixing oil and water in it. The petitioners- accused persons were involved in serious offence, which would affect the health of general public as well as small children. It is submitted that the petitioners-accused persons were absconding since from the date of incident and if they are released on bail, they may again abscond from the jurisdiction of trial court and they may not be available for trial. On these grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition.
